stem: Which pattern is most consistent with the duration, cross-setting, and functional-impairment features used in ADHD diagnostic criteria?

options.A: Inattention for 8 months at school, with no similar symptoms at home or in other settings.
options.B: Inattention or hyperactivity for 8 months at home and school, with clear impairment in daily functioning.
options.C: Inattention for 6 weeks at home and school after a major family disruption, with declining grades.
options.D: Inattention for 8 months at home and school, with age-appropriate functioning and no meaningful impairment.

rationale: CDC's current summary of DSM-5 criteria states that ADHD symptoms are present for at least 6 months, that several symptoms occur in two or more settings, and that there is clear evidence of interference with or reduced quality of social, school, or work functioning. B is the only option that includes all three features. A lacks cross-setting symptoms. C describes only 6 weeks and includes a major contextual stressor that requires consideration of other explanations. D explicitly lacks meaningful impairment and describes age-appropriate functioning. These features support recognition of the diagnostic pattern but do not by themselves establish an ADHD diagnosis; full evaluation also considers symptom count, age at onset, developmental appropriateness, and alternative explanations.
educational_objective: Recognize the ADHD diagnostic-pattern features of symptoms persisting at least 6 months, occurring in multiple settings, and causing functional impairment, while distinguishing these features from a complete diagnosis.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Care of ADHD in Children
source_locator: DSM-5 criteria for ADHD diagnosis: symptom-duration note (at least 6 months); 'In addition to the above criteria' bullets requiring symptoms in two or more settings and clear functional interference; 'Diagnosis and evaluation of ADHD' steps requiring assessment and ruling out other possible conditions.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance summarizing DSM-5 criteria supports the duration, cross-setting, functional-impairment, developmental-appropriateness, and alternative-explanation concepts used in the item.

source_original.stem: Which pattern most strongly supports further evaluation for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)?

options.A: Inattention for 8 months at school, with no similar symptoms at home or in other settings.
options.B: Inattention or hyperactivity for 8 months at home and school, with clear impairment in daily functioning.
options.C: Inattention for 6 weeks at home and school after a major family disruption, with declining grades.
options.D: Inattention for 8 months at home and school, with age-appropriate functioning and no meaningful impairment.

source_original.rationale: ADHD evaluation is supported by a persistent pattern lasting at least 6 months, occurring in at least two settings, and causing functional impairment. Option B includes all three features. A is limited to one setting, C is too brief and has an alternative contextual explanation, and D lacks impairment.
source_original.source_detail: CDC ADHD diagnostic criteria section: symptoms persist at least 6 months, are present in two or more settings, interfere with or reduce quality of social/school/work functioning, and are not better explained by another disorder. CDC Clinical Care of ADHD in Children dated 2026-07-30; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, professional boundaries, coping and psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Rewrote the stem because the original phrase 'supports further evaluation' was broad enough that a persistent single-setting symptom could also justify clinical assessment. The final stem explicitly tests the source-supported duration, cross-setting, and impairment features. Retained the original options and key B, and tightened the rationale to avoid implying that these three features alone establish an ADHD diagnosis.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC health-care-provider guidance summarizing DSM-5 criteria; NCSBN 2026 for blueprint mapping
audit_findings.currentness: CDC page updated/reviewed 2026-07-30 and live-rechecked 2026-08-16; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan current
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Clinical Care of ADHD in Children > DSM-5 criteria for ADHD diagnosis and Diagnosis and evaluation of ADHD; NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity > Mental Health Concepts, printed p.32
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only directly supported criteria features: at least 6 months, multiple settings, functional impairment, developmental appropriateness, and consideration of alternative explanations. It explicitly avoids treating these features alone as a complete diagnosis.

distractor_audit.A: Plausible persistent inattention but limited to one setting, so it lacks the cross-setting criterion tested by the stem.
distractor_audit.B: Correct: includes duration beyond 6 months, home and school settings, and clear impairment.
distractor_audit.C: Plausible impairment in two settings but only 6 weeks, and the major family disruption requires consideration of an alternative explanation.
distractor_audit.D: Has duration and multiple settings but explicitly lacks meaningful impairment and describes age-appropriate functioning.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: After the stem rewrite, only B contains all three features explicitly requested; no other option satisfies the construct.
audit_findings.cueing: All four options use parallel duration/setting/function descriptions; B is not identifiable by a unique technical term or implausible distractors.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity — mental-health concepts and recognition of clinically significant symptom patterns.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited the rewritten stem, all four options, key, rationale, objective, current CDC locator, NCSBN mapping, cueing, and second-answer risk from zero. B remained uniquely correct and no unsupported diagnostic claim remained.
